method: Semantic review performed by Claude (Claude Code) while authoring the corpus, encoded here as static rules with quoted evidence -- no external LLM API calls happen at run time. Matching includes paraphrased/implied mentions that share no keyword with the change (see mention_type=indirect).

affected_articles.evidence: each key can make up to 100 requests per minute across all endpoints
affected_articles.rationale: States the exact old limit that the change replaces.

affected_articles.evidence: if you're building a high-volume integration and start seeing frequent 429 responses, consider spreading requests across a longer window or batching calls
affected_articles.rationale: Assumes 429s are common enough to require batching advice; that assumption is calibrated to the old 100/min ceiling and reads as overly cautious once the limit is 500/min. No number or the phrase 'rate limit' appears.

affected_articles.evidence: if you're checking for updates more than once every second or two, you're a good candidate for webhooks instead of polling
affected_articles.rationale: The polling threshold implicitly reflects the old per-minute budget. Still technically safe advice, but understates how much headroom exists under the new limit.

could_not_assess.evidence: Enterprise includes custom contracts, dedicated support, SSO, and elevated API throughput beyond the standard per-key limit
could_not_assess.reason: Enterprise throughput is described as custom/negotiated and only 'beyond the standard limit' -- unclear whether raising the standard 100->500 limit changes what 'elevated' means here, or whether Enterprise numbers are independent. Needs a human (or a source-of-truth on Enterprise contracts) to resolve.

affected_articles.evidence: click the 'Export' button in the top toolbar
affected_articles.rationale: Names the exact button label being renamed.

affected_articles.evidence: uses the same generation process as clicking the export icon in the toolbar yourself
affected_articles.rationale: Refers back to the same toolbar control by its current (soon-to-be-old) name.

affected_articles.evidence: click the export icon at the top of the log to save the filtered results as a CSV file
affected_articles.rationale: A second, easy-to-miss instance of the same UI element in a different article -- the rename is app-wide, not just on the Exporting Your Data page.

affected_articles.evidence: it includes core features, community support, and 5GB of cloud storage per team
affected_articles.rationale: States the exact old Starter storage figure.

affected_articles.evidence: dropping down to the smaller allowance on the entry-level plan could put you over the cap
affected_articles.rationale: Warns that downgrading is risky because Starter storage is small; that risk is much lower once Starter is 20GB. No number is stated.

affected_articles.evidence: On the Starter plan, this allowance is 5GB per team
affected_articles.rationale: States the exact old Starter storage figure.

affected_articles.evidence: Endpoints created under our legacy v1 system receive unsigned XML payloads ... Both formats are currently supported side by side
affected_articles.rationale: Explicitly names v1 and states it is still supported, which becomes false once v1 is retired.

affected_articles.evidence: you may still be pointed at our original webhook endpoint format from early in Cascade's history -- these older connections continue to function for now
affected_articles.rationale: Describes v1 without ever naming it, and asserts it 'continues to function' -- exactly the claim the retirement invalidates.

affected_articles.evidence: the link is single-use and expires 24 hours after it's sent
affected_articles.rationale: States the exact old expiration window.

affected_articles.evidence: the reset link sent to your inbox will stay active for a while after it's issued, so there's no need to rush back to your email the moment you request it
affected_articles.rationale: Directly contradicts the new 1-hour window ('no need to rush') without ever stating a duration -- an unusually sharp example of an implied mention going stale.

could_not_assess.evidence: Once SSO is enabled, you can require it for all members, which disables password-based sign-in for your workspace
could_not_assess.reason: SSO-enforced workspaces disable password sign-in entirely, so the reset-link expiration change may be moot for this article's audience -- but it's a judgment call on scope, not a clear factual error, so it's not asserted as affected.

results.change_title: Editor Role Split into Editor and Contributor

affected_articles.evidence: Anyone you invite as an Editor today can create, modify, and delete any content in the workspace ... Editors currently have broad, unrestricted content permissions
affected_articles.rationale: Describes the pre-split, all-or-nothing Editor role and never uses the word 'Contributor' or states a role count -- purely behavioral description that goes stale once the role splits.

affected_articles.evidence: Cascade currently has four permission levels: Owner, Admin, Editor, and Viewer ... there currently isn't a role that draws that distinction
affected_articles.rationale: States the exact old role count/list and explicitly claims the gap that the new Contributor role fills no longer exists.
